responses.content: I will investigate the heap failure with GC, heap, cache source, and log evidence.

arguments.statement: An unbounded static cache in ReportCache retains every ReportEntry until the heap is exhausted.
cause_chain: ReportController.load serves each report through ReportService.getReport.
ReportCache.get inserts every loaded report into a static ConcurrentHashMap.
The map has no eviction or size bound, so live data grows until java.lang.OutOfMemoryError.

requirements.description: The GC log shows repeated Full GCs that cannot recover the heap.
The live heap histogram is dominated by cached report objects.
The indexed source shows an unbounded static cache insertion.
Same-thread log context shows the report load followed by the heap failure.

falsifiers: Surviving heap is small and the dominant class is unrelated to the cache.
Full GCs recover most of the heap after each collection.

arguments.statement: The 2 GiB heap is undersized for the report workload.
cause_chain: The workload serves more concurrent reports than the configured heap can hold.
Available heap is exhausted during a burst.
The process fails with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError even though objects are later reclaimable.

requirements.description: Full GC events show the heap recovering substantially after collection.

falsifiers: Most of the heap remains live after Full GC, indicating retained objects.

arguments.statement: A single oversized report payload triggers the allocation failure.
cause_chain: One request loads an unusually large report.
The allocation cannot fit in the remaining heap.
The request thread fails with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError.

requirements.description: The heap histogram shows one class or one huge allocation dominating the heap.

falsifiers: The heap is dominated by many small cached instances rather than one large object.

responses.content: I will assess the GC, heap, source, and log evidence for the cache hypothesis.

assessments.rationale: Four Full GCs in fifteen seconds reclaim only 47 MB at the end and leave about 1.9 GB live.
ReportEntry dominates live bytes with 1,150,000 instances, and ConcurrentHashMap$Node is the third-largest class.
The static CACHE map receives every loaded report with no eviction, TTL, or size limit.
The same request thread logs report load, cache-size warning, and the heap failure in order.

responses.content: I will assess the undersized-heap and single-large-object alternatives.

assessments.rationale: The final Full GC reclaims only 47 MB and leaves roughly 1.9 GB live, so the failure is retained data rather than a temporarily undersized heap.
The dominant class is 1,150,000 small ReportEntry instances, not a single oversized allocation.

responses.content: The unbounded cache hypothesis is confirmed. I will propose grounded remediation.

actions.title: Bound the report cache with eviction and TTL
actions.description: Replace the unbounded static ConcurrentHashMap in ReportCache with a bounded cache such as Caffeine with a maximum weight or entry count and an expiry policy. Ensure the cache is shared safely and metrics expose size and eviction counts.
actions.risk: Excess eviction can increase report load latency and database pressure.
prerequisites: Measure report cache hit ratio and service heap budget
verification_steps: Replay the report workload under load and confirm heap stays below budget
Check cache hit ratio and p99 latency after enabling eviction

actions.title: Add a cache-bound regression test
actions.description: Add a test that inserts more reports than the configured bound and asserts the cache size never exceeds it and evicted entries are reloaded.
actions.target: Add a ReportCache bound regression test
verification_steps: Run the cache test in CI with a fixed entry limit
